I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked last year and only change a little. Here in Quzhou, wheat and maize are still my main food and cash backbone, and with 15 mu total plus well water, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Cotton takes more watching and more picking, and with some people working off-farm, I will not put too much land into it. I finished middle school, so I do look at cost, fertilizer balance, and water, not just habit. But I still trust what I see locally. If the neighbors are putting enough fertilizer to hold yield, I will not cut too hard. Losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. So this year I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and 5 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, base fertilizer with more phosphorus, and give about 2 irrigations if the year is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, feed it heavier on nitrogen, and water around 2 times with the well. For cotton, I will keep fertilizer steady, not too low, and water about 3 times because if cotton dries at the wrong time, boll setting suffers. I will use rotary tillage on the wheat-maize land for speed and labor saving, and plough the cotton land because cotton roots better in looser ground. I am aiming for stable yield first, then cost control second.
